construct: Most Friedreich ataxia results from biallelic intronic GAA-repeat expansions that reduce FXN transcription and frataxin. Frataxin deficiency impairs mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, disrupts respiratory-chain and aconitase function, mislocalizes iron, and increases oxidative stress.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Progressive ataxia with proprioceptive loss, areflexia, cardiomyopathy, and biallelic FXN GAA expansions identifies Friedreich ataxia; reduced frataxin impairs mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Tay-Sachs, peroxisomal disease, PMP22 neuropathy, and Menkes are legitimate neurologic/metabolic alternatives but do not match the explicit FXN GAA-repeat mechanism or iron-sulfur-cluster defect.
